title: United Autosports edges G-Drive at the Red Bull Ring
dek: Filipe Albuquerque, Will Owen and Hugo de Sadeleer won the 4 Hours of Red Bull Ring for United's Ligier by 4.554 seconds, holding off pole-sitting G-Drive after a late fuel stop.

chapters.title: A title fight and a new Dallara
text: The 4 Hours of Red Bull Ring on 23 July 2017 was the third round of the European Le Mans Series, and the first season of the new-generation LMP2 formula had already produced two different winners. United Autosports took the opener at Silverstone with its Ligier JS P217, and G-Drive Racing's Oreca 07 won at Monza, where DragonSpeed's second car finished runner-up. The G-Drive crew arrived leading the points by 11 over United, with the DragonSpeed-run #21 trio of Henrik Hedman, Nicolas Lapierre and Ben Hanley third after gearbox trouble cost them at Silverstone.

The 36-car entry included 13 LMP2s, the most varied top-class field of the year: five Ligiers, four Orecas and four Dallaras. The newcomer was the #27 SMP Racing Dallara P217, fresh from the Le Mans 24 Hours, which made its ELMS debut with the Formula V8 3.5 pair of Egor Orudzhev and Matevos Isaakyan, neither of whom had driven an LMP2 car before and who had no testing in it. Further changes affected three crews. Nicolas Minassian replaced Ryo Hirakawa in the G-Drive #22 because the Japanese driver was racing at Sugo in Super GT, Olivier Pla took over from David Zollinger in the IDEC Sport #28 Ligier for the rest of the year, and Gustavo Yacaman joined the Graff #40 Oreca in place of Franck Matelli. Filipe Albuquerque, meanwhile, arrived with a fortnight of chassis-hopping behind him, having driven a Rebellion Oreca in the WEC on the previous weekend. After a thunderstorm on Thursday night the track was dry on Friday, but the forecast for race day carried a growing threat of storms.

chapters.title: Roussel beats Lapierre by five thousandths
text: DragonSpeed had topped both practice sessions through Lapierre, whose 1:19.082 in the second 90-minute session on Saturday morning was 1.3 seconds quicker than his Friday best. Qualifying, though, went to the sister car. In a ten-minute session Léo Roussel put the G-Drive #22 on pole with a 1:18.435, with Lapierre in the #21 just 0.005 behind on 1:18.440 after track-limits infringements cost him laps. It gave DragonSpeed a front-row lock-out.

Albuquerque was the best of the Ligiers in third on 1:18.834, around four tenths off the Orecas, with Nathanaël Berthon fourth in the Panis Barthez Competition Ligier #23 on 1:19.605. Orudzhev put the SMP Dallara #27 fifth on 1:19.746 in the team's maiden session, ahead of Yacaman's Graff #40, Pla's IDEC Ligier and Andrea Pizzitola in the Algarve Pro Ligier #25. The Graff #39 that had taken pole at Monza could do no better than 13th, a best of 1:24.461 leaving Enzo Guibbert more than five seconds from the top and with plenty of work to do on Sunday.

chapters.title: A three-way fight for the lead
text: At the 13:00 start Lapierre slipped from second to fourth in the opening laps. The lead then moved between the United Ligier, the G-Drive Oreca and the SMP Dallara, which opted for a different pit strategy from the rest of the LMP2 field and ran at the front on several occasions before stopping early in the second hour. Behind them the Graff #39, which started 13th, began to work its way through as others hit trouble.

chapters.title: Traffic, a stopped Oreca and a Full Course Yellow
text: In the middle of the race Minassian charged from fifth to the lead in the G-Drive, though he said later that he lost at least seven seconds over several laps behind a car that would not let him past. That slower car was the Algarve Pro Ligier #25, which he said was weaving in front of him. The delay allowed United back into the fight.

The race's only Full Course Yellow came with about an hour to go, when Hedman stopped the #21 DragonSpeed Oreca on track at Turn 8; the car never got back to Hanley and finished not classified. The SMP Dallara lost about three minutes in the pits and fell out of the fight for the podium, although its crew finished on the road in fifth.

chapters.title: A splash of fuel decides it
text: The winner was settled at the final round of stops. G-Drive had stopped several laps earlier than United, but Albuquerque's late pit stop for fuel, with 18 minutes left, was quick enough for him to emerge with a lead of about 12 seconds over Roussel. The Oreca was the quicker car in the closing stages and the gap came down from more than 10 seconds to 4.554 at the flag, with Roussel unable to find a way past before the end. Albuquerque said he had traffic problems of his own and worried about his tyres, but felt sure of the win over the last five laps.

Behind the two leaders Graff scored a quiet but productive result, with Guibbert, Eric Trouillet and Paul Petit taking third in the #39 and Richard Bradley, James Allen and Yacaman fourth in the #40, both on the same lap, one down on the winner. Panis Barthez Competition was fifth and SMP sixth, two laps behind.

chapters.title: Four points between G-Drive and United
text: It was the second win of the season for the #32 United crew, after Silverstone, and it cut the G-Drive crew's championship lead from 11 points to four with three races remaining. Albuquerque said the Ligier in sprint specification matched up well against the Oreca, which he took as a good sign for the rest of the season. Minassian, deputising for Hirakawa, left frustrated but pleased with the pace, saying the G-Drive car had been the best in practice, qualifying and the race.

In the revised classification the SMP Dallara dropped from fifth to sixth after a post-race time penalty, which put Panis Barthez Competition into fifth ahead of it. Racing Team Nederland was seventh and High Class Racing eighth, ten laps down. Tockwith Motorsports' Ligier #34 was classified 26th, Algarve Pro's #25 and the Cetilar Villorba Corse Dallara #47 were not classified, and neither was the IDEC Ligier #28.

The result had consequences beyond the points. Within two days United was the only team to have officially confirmed an entry for the 2018 Rolex 24 at Daytona, with Owen to share its Ligier with Lando Norris, and several ELMS teams including Graff, Algarve Pro, Cetilar Villorba Corse and IDEC were weighing up entries for IMSA's Florida events. Tockwith later shelved its prototype programme for the rest of the season, which brought the Le Castellet entry down to 35 cars.
The next round, the fourth of six, was the 4 Hours of Le Castellet at Paul Ricard on 27 August.

facts.v: Léo Roussel's 1:18.435 in the G-Drive Oreca beat team-mate Lapierre by 0.005 seconds, and was described as the closest pole battle in ELMS history.
